text:
GitHub Copilot CLI just shipped a plugins dashboard, and it's the exact thing we hand-wired live on our last stream.

What changed: Copilot CLI now ships a plugins dashboard with /plugin, /mcp, and /skills built in -- no more separately configuring an MCP server and hoping the environment finds it.

What it does: one place to see and manage every tool your agent can reach, an image model, a database, your own scripts, instead of scattered config files.

Why builders should care: on our 24-hour livestream we manually wired an MCP server into Copilot CLI just to get it talking to an image model for a batch of visuals. That whole setup is now a couple of commands.

Try this this week: open your CLI, run /mcp, and see what's already listed. Connect one real tool you use daily and let the agent reach it directly.

The bigger signal: the glue code keeps disappearing. The edge isn't wiring the plumbing anymore -- it's knowing what to plug in and why.

Save this for your AI stack.

text:
Most people get stuck at the same stage of the AI era without realizing there are four.

Consumer: watches the demos, never opens the tool.
Operator: uses it well, but only inside someone else's prompt.
Builder: ships something real -- the workflow becomes yours.
Frontier: builds systems other people learn from.

GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, a CLI that plugs into anything now -- none of it moves you up a stage by itself. Only building does.

We put together a simple map of the jump from operator to builder -- the exact moves, not theory.
